content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces a new model for balancing the trade-off between modelling efficiency and the capacity of visual attention. This is pursued mainly by multi-step interactions and a new strategy to construct queries and keys based on bipartite graphs. The authors claim to achieve competitive results with 15% fewer parameters and 10-25% less computation with their method on several vision tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Main Strengths:
- The paper tackles a relevant problem aiming to make transformers networks less computationally intensive.
- The proposed methodology seems to be original and principled.

Main Weaknesses:

- Tables 1 and 2 are not referred to in the text. Moreover, the captions could present more details about their content. Therefore, it is hard to follow what the results are showing exactly. For instance, in Tab. 1, the first group of original methods (FCN, ICNet, etc.) is compared with the original version of Segformer and also its modified versions (with RWGKA). It is not clear what the authors are trying to show exactly. The overall experiments and results are not clearly presented in Sec. 4, making it hard for the reader to follow.

Suggestions:
For the sake of completeness on transformers and efficient transformers approaches, the authors could include references to the STTN [1] and FastSTTN [2] methods.

References:
[1] Zeng, Y. et al., Learning Joint Spatial-Temporal Transformations for Video Inpainting, ECCV 2020.
[2] Escher, R. et al., Fast Spatial-Temporal Transformer Network, SIBGRAPI 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The proposed methodology is clear and sound. It seems to be a novel approach yet inspired by Zaheer et al. (2020). However, the quality of the presentation of experiments and results could be improved. The authors claim that the code will be made publicly available.
content.summary_of_the_review: I believe the experimental part of the paper lacks organization and clarity, raising some concerns about its acceptance. Although the proposed method is relevant and novel, the presented results suggest the paper could be improved and resubmitted to an upcoming conference.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper focuses on reducing quadratic computational complexity of self-attention module. Instead of onestep interaction between nodes, the paper utilizes random work graph kernel to model multi-step node interaction. To keep a linear time complexity, a new strategy to construct queries and keys based on bipartite graph is proposed. The effectiveness of our approach is verified on various visual tasks including segmentation, image quantization and image classification.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- The idea to utilize random walk graph kernel for multi-step interaction is reasonable.
- The complexity of the proposed method is kept at linear level by introducing a bipartite graph.
- The effectiveness and generalization of our approach is verified on various visual tasks.


Weaknesses:
- The ablation study is not fully conducted: 1) comparison with linear attention methods [1,2] on various visual tasks. 2) Using random walk graph kernel and bipartite graph is somewhat complex, why not use some simpler operations such as those in [3,4].
- The experimental results on segmentation do not show much improvement. For example, Segformer-RWGKA (MiT-B1-RWKA) only decrease FLOPs by 25% but leads to 0.4% accuracy drop. Network pruning methods [5,6] can achieve similar or better performance. Could you compare with pruning methods?

[1] Katharopoulos, Angelos, et al. "Transformers are rnns: Fast autoregressive transformers with linear attention." International Conference on Machine Learning. PMLR, 2020.

[2] Wang, Sinong, et al. "Linformer: Self-attention with linear complexity." arXiv preprint arXiv:2006.04768 (2020).

[3] Han, Kai, et al. "Vision GNN: An Image is Worth Graph of Nodes." arXiv preprint arXiv:2206.00272 (2022).

[4] Yu, Weihao, et al. "Metaformer is actually what you need for vision." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2022.

[5] Liu, Zhuang, et al. "Learning efficient convolutional networks through network slimming." Proceedings of the IEEE international conference on computer vision. 2017.

[6] He, Yihui, et al. "Amc: Automl for model compression and acceleration on mobile devices." Proceedings of the European conference on computer vision (ECCV). 2018.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well organized and easy to follow. The idea to utilize random walk graph kernel for multi-step interaction is reasonable and basically novel. The authors say that code will be made publicly available, so that the reproducibility will be guaranteed.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper proposes a new attention module with random walk graph kernel. The idea is reasonable but the experimental benefit is not significant, so I give a score 5: marginally below the acceptance threshold. content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This work addresses the challenge of high complexity in vision transformers, namely the quadratic complexity in computing cross-neuron attention. The key ideas include: (1) use "anchors" to change the size of K and Q in the attention operator, implemented by the multiplication of some additional learnable parameters. (2) propose a random walk graph kernel for incorporating "long-distance" interaction among neurons with a same layer of transformer. Various experiments are conducted on validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, such as image classification on ImageNet-1K.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 

- The topic is of crucial importance for large neural models, given that most of state-of-the-art neural backbones are now transformer based. Reducing the quadratic complexity of K-Q-V operation, without much sacrifice of performance, can significantly accelerate the large models such as BERT.

- The proposed method is clearly explained, including its technical designs, the complexity and corresponding experiments.

Weakness:

- The experiments indeed do not fully support the main claims.

- The proposed idea of "anchor" graph can be shown to be equivalent to the original attention.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: I do not have any complaint about the clarity of this submission.
Quality: Overall it bring some new idea (e.g., graph kernel). However, it is not fully justified by empirical studies. 
Reproducibility: The proposed method is not sophisticated and built based on existing transformer models such as ViL, thus I believe most readers can re-implement it.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The paper proposed two ideas for improving the transformers. The first one is to introduce the random walk graph kernel, which adds terms like lambda^n A^n to the original attention matrix A. with an observation that properly choosing lambda can ensure some property (Lemma 1). The belief is that higher-order terms can capture long-distance affect among different neurons in an attention module. The second idea is to use "anchor" points in order to reducing the size of matrices K and Q. To this end, two additional parameter matrices are multiplied to K, Q respectively. 

My major concern is that, both ideas does not really make sense. For the first idea, the experiments do not fully support. For example, looking into Table 5, by varying lambda (from 0.1 to 0.9, higher lambda emphasizes higher-order terms), one can notice good performances favors lower lambda (i.e., A itself plays a more important role). The performance discrepancy among using different lambdas are too minor to draw some convincing conclusions. 

For the second idea, Since B_Q, B_K are both linear operators, they can be merged with W_Q, W_K respectively and treated as a single matrix. From the experiments, it is not clear on which aspects the anchor idea does help. The GFLOPs are not reduced to a large extent.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to improve the linear attention in efficient Transformers with Random Walk Graph Kernel (RWGK). The motivation is to achieve a better trade-off between accuracy and efficiency in the linear setting. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[ Strength ]
+ The motivation of improving the performance of linear attention is clear and necessary. Indeed, standard Transformers suffer from the quadratic complexity, which prevents it from adapting to longer sequences. Linear attention can improve the efficiency but the accuracy is sacrificed. Achieving a better trade-off between efficiency and accuracy is currently a hot topic in research.
+ The introduced RWGK technique is simple and effective. RWGK is not a new technique, but it can be seamlessly applied into the linear attention to facilitate the more precise and sufficient interaction between tokens. Notably, RWGK does not involve too many parameters and computational burden. Additionally, it is a plug-and-play technique that can be conveniently applied to exiting Transformer backbones.
+ Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method in speeding up the computational speed and achieving comparable performance. 

[ Weakness ]
- The method is lack of originality and novelty. It is quite common to combine a classical method with new structures, but the presentation in this paper is not very attractive. For example, it does not give solid analysis on the degraded performance of linear attention, in which case the motivation of using RWGK is not very clear. More insights should be emphasized here.
- From Table 4, it looks like that the efficiency (FLOPs) is not significantly improved. Why does this occur? Also, FLOPs only reveals the theoretical efficiency, so it would be better to compare the actual throughput (e.g., fps).
- The method should be validated on all the mentioned three linear attention types, i.e., sparse patterns, low-rank approximation, and kernel-based approximation.
- The literature is generally out-of-date. The paper should include more 2022 papers, and apply the method to these new baselines.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is generally clear and logical, but it lacks of some originality.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering the points in [ Weakness ], I would expect the authors to carefully improve the paper.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to linearly approximate the quadratic self-attention mechanism to reduce the computational cost and memory footprint on long sequence input. By introducing a multi-step interaction between graph nodes, the enhanced self-attention, i.e., RWGKA as termed in the paper, is equivalent to finding the inverse matrix as in random walk graph kernel, and with the bipartite graph, the proposed approach can achieve linear complexity. The experimental results on various computer vision tasks approve the effectiveness of the approach.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1) The idea of enhancing self-attention by considering multi-step interaction is novel and the mathematical derivation is elegant.
2) Compared to the efficient attention, the proposel random walk graph kernel attention improves the modeling capacity by considering hierarchical relative interactions instead of only one-step interaction between queries and keys.
3) The results on semantic segmentation task show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Weakness:

1) Built on top of the simple linear attention, the proposed approach only compares with the simple linear attention on image quantization task, whereas there is no comparison with other linear attention variants such as linformer, performer, axial attention, multi axis attention on image classification, object detection, image segmentation tasks, which is hard to prove its generalization ability. Also, authors need to clarify what's the difference between the base anchors of bipartite graph in this work and the projection on token dimension in linformer, and the spatial reduction attention in PVT, these three are quite similar.
2) As shown in the recent work MetaFormer, the quadratic self-attention mechanism is not critical to performance, but rather the overall architecture combined with layer norm and residual connection ensures the lower bound of performance, hence, whether or not linearizing the self-attention worths the research effort is still worth further discussion.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The quality is good with minor spelling mistakes, how the bipartite graph improves the capacity and effiency of the attention matrix is a bit unclear, and the work is novel in terms of originality.
content.summary_of_the_review: The idea is novel, the experimental result is somewhat convicing, the comparison with other linear self-attention variants on other tasks needs to be added to give a thorough comparison.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 4: The contributions are significant, and do not exist in prior works.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 4: The contributions are significant, and do not exist in prior works.
